questions.prompt: Walk the 3439 per-key merge decision through the worked trace. How does each key in the example get its outcome?

keyPoints.text: Absence is the deletion encoding - a deleted key is simply not an own property.
keyPoints.quote: Deletion is represented by an absent own property.

keyPoints.text: When both sides diverge from base and from each other, the key is conflicted and local's state is kept.
keyPoints.quote: record a conflict and take local

keyPoints.text: A conflicted local deletion drops the key from the merged value but still lists it by name.
keyPoints.quote: removes the key while retaining its name

keyPoints.text: In the trace, note is exactly that case: local deleted it while remote revised it.
title stays 'edited' because remote still matches base, proving remote never moved.
The trace deliberately separates three distinct questions instead of one clever expression.
keyPoints.quote: which keys participate, whether each record owns a key, and which comparison selects the final state

questions.prompt: What does nullish coalescing actually guarantee, and why is a string fallback still the wrong absence encoding here?

keyPoints.text: ?? keeps the empty string; it only falls back for null and undefined.
|| is the operator that loses empty strings, because it reacts to every falsy value.
keyPoints.quote: Logical OR falls back for every falsy value, including the empty string.

keyPoints.text: A string sentinel lives inside the value domain, so collisions are possible by construction.
keyPoints.quote: the input domain permits every string

keyPoints.text: Once a stored value equals the fallback, deletion and data become indistinguishable.
keyPoints.quote: Missing and a stored fallback string would compare equal.

keyPoints.text: Plain bracket lookup can also read values off the prototype chain, which no fallback choice fixes.
keyPoints.quote: also reads inherited values, so changing the fallback does not address property ownership

keyPoints.text: A unique symbol keeps absence outside the domain and survives a later widening of the contract.
keyPoints.quote: A fresh symbol makes that separation explicit

questions.prompt: Explain the output-construction boundary: why Object.fromEntries, and what are the cost and cloning limits of the result?

keyPoints.text: Building the result from entries makes even '__proto__' an ordinary own data key.
keyPoints.quote: That creates an own data property

keyPoints.text: Assigning to result.__proto__ goes through the inherited setter instead of defining data.
keyPoints.quote: it does not reliably create the desired data property

keyPoints.text: With a string on the right-hand side, that setter call is a silent no-op, not a prototype swap.
keyPoints.quote: For a string value it is ignored, rather than replacing the prototype with a string.

keyPoints.text: Diagnosing special-key failures requires looking at the value's type, not just the key's name.
One up-front sort of the key union is what makes the conflicts list lexicographic.
keyPoints.quote: The union of own keys is sorted once, so conflicts are lexicographic.

keyPoints.text: The merge allocates a fresh output object but can share the strings themselves.
keyPoints.quote: need not deeply clone values because the permitted values are strings
